name: Micron Batu Kawan assembly and test facility, Penang
aliases: Micron Penang second assembly and test facility

parties.name: Micron Technology
parties.note: Runs the site through its Malaysian subsidiary Micron Memory Malaysia Sdn. Bhd., incorporated in October 2018.

summary: Micron's assembly and test site in Batu Kawan Industrial Park, Penang, built to supply NAND, PC DRAM and SSD modules. Micron announced it in November 2018 as a greenfield SSD assembly and test site with a planned RM1.5 billion over five years and 1,000 local jobs, aiming to break ground in the first half of 2019. On 13 October 2023 Micron inaugurated a new assembly and test facility there, which Penang's chief minister called an expansion of the Batu Kawan site; Micron said it would add up to another USD 1 billion for construction and full equipping, on top of USD 1 billion already invested in Penang, raising factory space to 1.5 million square feet. The law firm that advised on the first two phases puts the development's indicative cost at about USD 2 billion on about 52.6 acres. Micron says the facility uses smart manufacturing and follows the LEED green building rating system.

metrics.note: Planned investment over five years for the new SSD assembly and test site, given in the 2018 release as USD 357 million.

notes: Micron's 2023 release quotes Penang's chief minister calling the new facility an expansion of Micron's Batu Kawan site, and a law firm describes the development in two phases, so this record covers the whole Batu Kawan site; no source read here dates the start of construction or of production in the first phase, so the status rests on the 2023 opening. Trade press calls the 2023 facility Micron's second Penang plant, after one in the Perai industrial area that it says opened in 2015, and estimates USD 2 billion invested and 4,500 jobs across the two sites, while the law firm gives about USD 2 billion for the Batu Kawan development alone; the sources do not reconcile these figures with each other or with the 2018 ringgit budget. The Edge Malaysia article first appeared in its weekly edition of 15 to 21 March 2021. A November 2026 search found no newer source specific to this site.

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Claude): re-opened every cited source, checked each statement against it and searched for newer reporting.
review.changes: Reframed the record as the two-phase Batu Kawan site after Micron's release described the 2023 facility as an expansion of that site, adding a law firm's note on both phases (USD 2 billion, 52.6 acres) and a 2021 report on the subsidiary and construction timing; marked the 4,500 jobs estimate as approximate. Audit fixes (2026-11-07): removed the word initial from the 2018 RM1.5 billion plan, which the 2018 release does not use, and dropped an unsupported attribution of the trade press report to Bernama.
